7ccead5340.q: What is the £100,000 per head revenue rule for scaling a mortgage business?
7ccead5340.a: The rule of thumb is that you should aim for £100,000 pounds per head revenue. As one person, you want to try and get to £100,000. As two people, you want to try and get to £200,000. If you have two part-time people, that's one full-time person. When you've got three, that is £200,000. If you're a team of 10 and you're not doing at least a million pounds per year, you need to fix your leaky bucket and get your team working more efficiently.

0175fde664.q: How should you track your time before hiring your first team member?
0175fde664.a: Before you hire anyone, you need to track every hour for at least two weeks using a spreadsheet that runs from 8 AM until whatever time you finish (like 8 PM for 12-hour days). You go through and work out exactly what you're doing in half-hour or hour increments throughout that whole two-week period, putting things into four buckets: new business, advice, post-sale application, and working on the business. The highest value activity is working on your business, while the other three buckets are the ones eating you alive.

592ad2b46c.q: What are the three questions to ask before hiring your first admin or advisor?
592ad2b46c.a: Number one, can you afford it based on the written business that you've done over the last three months? Number two, will it free up the time that earns more money—like if you've got protection sitting on your desk or if you're doing too much administration? And number three, have the role written down in specific tasks, actions, and techniques that you want them to put into place. That is vital.
